To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the Eastern California shear system accommodates ∼18 km of dextrally sheared crust across the Mojave Desert, and that this shear is transferred to the Garlock Fault.
the Eastern California shear Zone accommodates ∼ 18 km of dextrally offset across the central Mojav Desert, which is transferred northward along the Garlock fault to the Walker Lane belt.

the central Mojave portion of the Eastern shear zone accommodates 25% of the Pacific–North American plate boundary dextral shear and is transferred northward into the Walker Lane belt via clockwise rotation of the trace of the Garlock fault.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the distribution of slip across the central Mojove Desert portion of the eastern California shear zone.
the distribution of dextral deformation in the central Mojove Desert.

(1) the distribution of dextral offset along faults in the central part of the Mojave Desert; (2) the amount of dextrall slip accommodated by faults in the central portion of the Eastern shear zone; (3) the amount of fault slip accommodated by the Blackwater and Harper Lake faults, the major faults of the central Mojave desert; and (4) the amount of total dextral slip across the central Mojaves Desert.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the central Mojave fault system accommodates ∼18 km of dextrally sheared crust, and this slip is transferred to the Garlock Fault, which accommodates ∼22 km of slip.

the Eastern California shear-zone is a through-going fault system that accommodates a significant proportion of the Pacific-North American plate boundary shear, and the Garlock fault is the northern terminus of this system.

the Eastern California shear system has accommodated 18 ± 4 km of dextrally transcurrent motion, and that the Garlock fault has accommodated 7 ± 4 km, with 11 ± 6 km of dextraly transcurrent motion accommodated in the Walker Lane belt, since 3.8 ± 1 Ma.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the Garlock fault and the Eastern California shear-zone faults accommodate through-going dextrally shearing, and the Walker Lane belt accommodates the majority of the dextral shear in the region.
